questions.question: The Giapetto production LP chooses weekly numbers $x_s$ of wooden soldiers and $x_t$ of trains and maximizes $z=3x_s+2x_t$. What does the coefficient 3 represent?
options: The selling price of one soldier, before material and labour costs are deducted
The number of finishing hours that one soldier needs in the workshop
The total weekly profit earned from all soldiers made in that week
Profit per soldier: its revenue minus the material and labour costs it causes

questions.question: Giapetto's LP for weekly soldiers $x_s$ and trains $x_t$ has a finishing constraint $2x_s+x_t\le100$, a carpentry constraint $x_s+x_t\le80$ and a demand constraint $x_s\le40$. Why does only one of these contain $x_s$ alone?
options: Finishing time is used by soldiers only, so trains drop out of that constraint.
Carpentry is a soldier-only resource, so its constraint omits the trains.
The demand limit concerns soldier sales only; trains have no such limit.
Soldiers earn more per unit, so the model caps the more profitable product.

questions.question: In Giapetto's LP, $x_s$ and $x_t$ are the numbers of soldiers and trains made per week, and finishing time is limited by $2x_s+x_t\le100$. What do the numbers 2, 1 and 100 mean?
options: Total labour hours per soldier and per train, and all labour hours available
Soldiers finished per hour, trains finished per hour, and finishing hours available
Profit per soldier, profit per train, and the finishing hours available
Finishing hours per soldier, finishing hours per train, and finishing hours available

questions.question: In Giapetto's LP for weekly soldiers $x_s$ and trains $x_t$, the soldier constraint is $x_s\le40$. What practical requirement does it represent?
options: At least 40 soldiers must be made each week to meet customer orders.
Exactly 40 soldiers are made each week, and only trains are chosen.
At most 40 soldiers can be sold weekly, so making more is pointless.
At most 40 hours per week are available for making the soldiers.

questions.question: Giapetto's LP maximizes $3x_s+2x_t$ over weekly numbers $x_s$ of soldiers and $x_t$ of trains, subject to $2x_s+x_t\le100$, $x_s+x_t\le80$, $x_s\le40$ and $x_s,x_t\ge0$, with no further restrictions. What does this formulation allow for $x_s$ and $x_t$?
options: Only whole numbers, since an LP never allows fractional toys
Only values that the LP solver rounds to whole numbers afterwards
Any nonnegative values meeting the constraints, fractions too
Only whole numbers, since integrality is a linear constraint

questions.question: Giapetto makes $x_s$ soldiers and $x_t$ trains per week, subject to finishing hours $2x_s+x_t\le100$, carpentry hours $x_s+x_t\le80$ and soldier demand $x_s\le40$, with $x_s,x_t\ge0$. Is the plan of 30 soldiers and 45 trains feasible?
options: Yes: it needs only 75 of the 80 carpentry hours.
Yes: 30 soldiers are within the demand limit of 40.
No: it needs 105 finishing hours, more than 100.
No: it needs 85 carpentry hours, more than 80.

questions.question: Giapetto's weekly profit is $3x_s+2x_t$ for $x_s$ soldiers and $x_t$ trains, subject to $2x_s+x_t\le100$ (finishing), $x_s+x_t\le80$ (carpentry), $x_s\le40$ (demand) and $x_s,x_t\ge0$. What can be said about the plan $(x_s,x_t)=(40,20)$?
options: Infeasible, since $x_s\le40$ excludes 40
Feasible, with weekly profit 140
Infeasible: finishing uses all 100 hours
Feasible, with weekly profit 160

questions.question: In Giapetto's LP, $x_s$ soldiers and $x_t$ trains are made per week, and the objective $3x_s+2x_t$ uses profit contributions per unit. A soldier's selling price rises by 2 while all unit costs stay the same. What is the new objective?

Giapetto plans to make 30 soldiers and 40 trains per week. Finishing allows $2x_s+x_t\le100$ hours, carpentry $x_s+x_t\le80$ hours and demand $x_s\le40$, where $x_s$ and $x_t$ count soldiers and trains. Which constraints bind at this plan?
options: Only finishing binds; 10 carpentry hours stay unused.
Finishing and carpentry both bind at this plan.
Only carpentry binds; 30 finishing hours stay unused.
Only demand binds, since 30 soldiers are made.

questions.question: Giapetto, making $x_s$ soldiers and $x_t$ trains per week, adds a rule that it may make at most twice as many trains as soldiers. Which constraint expresses the rule, and what does it imply for the plan $(x_s,x_t)=(20,60)$?
options: $x_t\le2x_s$, which $(20,60)$ meets as $20\le120$
$2x_t\le x_s$, which caps trains at half the soldiers
$x_s\le2x_t$, which caps soldiers at twice the trains
$x_t\le2x_s$, which $(20,60)$ violates as $60>40$

questions.question: Giapetto's optimal weekly plan makes $x_s=20$ soldiers and $x_t=60$ trains, while the demand constraint is $x_s\le40$. What does the slack of 20 in this constraint mean?
options: The plan violates soldier demand by 20, so it is not actually feasible.
20 fewer soldiers are made than could be sold; demand does not bind here.
20 customers who want soldiers are not served, so demand is unmet.
20 soldiers are made but stay unsold at the end of the week.

questions.question: In Giapetto's LP, maximize $3x_s+2x_t$, the contributions 3 and 2 are revenue minus material and labour cost per soldier and per train. A student also subtracts $c(2x_s+x_t)$, the cost $c$ per hour of finishing labour used. Is that correct?
options: Yes; every hour of labour used reduces profit, so it must appear in the objective.
No; finishing labour is already in the unit contributions and would count twice.
Yes; the finishing constraint limits hours but does not price them in the model.
No; costs belong in the constraints, and only revenues belong in the objective.

questions.question: Giapetto earns $3x_s+2x_t$ per week from $x_s$ soldiers and $x_t$ trains, with finishing $2x_s+x_t\le100$, carpentry $x_s+x_t\le80$, demand $x_s\le40$ and $x_s,x_t\ge0$. Among the plans $(40,20)$, $(20,60)$, $(0,80)$ and $(30,45)$, which feasible plan earns the most?

In Giapetto's LP (maximize $3x_s+2x_t$ subject to $2x_s+x_t\le100$, $x_s+x_t\le80$, $x_s\le40$, $x_s,x_t\ge0$), the optimal plan is $(x_s,x_t)=(20,60)$. A new rule requires at least 30 trains per week. What is the optimal plan now?
options: A new plan with less profit, since every extra rule costs profit
Still $(20,60)$: it meets the rule, and the region only shrank
None, since the rule makes $(20,60)$ infeasible
A new plan with more profit, since more trains are now made

questions.question: Giapetto's finishing capacity rises from 100 to 110 hours, so the constraints become $2x_s+x_t\le110$, $x_s+x_t\le80$ and $x_s\le40$ for weekly soldiers $x_s$ and trains $x_t$. Which plan uses all finishing hours and all carpentry hours?

In Giapetto's LP, soldiers earn 3 and trains 2 per unit; a soldier needs 2 finishing hours and a train 1, both need 1 carpentry hour, with 100 finishing and 80 carpentry hours and at most 40 soldiers. Why is it not best to make as many soldiers as possible?
options: Per scarce finishing hour a soldier earns only 1.5, while a train earns 2.
The demand limit of 40 soldiers forces the rest of the capacity onto trains.
Per carpentry hour a train earns more than a soldier, so trains are preferred.
Profit depends on the number of toys made, and trains allow more toys.

questions.question: Giapetto maximizes $3x_s+2x_t$ subject to finishing $2x_s+x_t\le100$, carpentry $x_s+x_t\le80$, demand $x_s\le40$ and $x_s,x_t\ge0$, with optimal plan $(20,60)$ and profit 180. If the demand limit is deleted, why is $(20,60)$ still optimal?
options: A demand limit never affects the optimal plan in any production model.
Adding the finishing and carpentry hour limits caps every plan's profit at 180.
Deleting any constraint always leaves the old optimal plan optimal.
It is not; without the limit $(50,0)$ becomes feasible and earns more.

questions.question: Suppose Giapetto's soldier contribution rises to 4, so it maximizes $4x_s+2x_t$ subject to $2x_s+x_t\le100$, $x_s+x_t\le80$, $x_s\le40$ and $x_s,x_t\ge0$. Which statement about the old optimal plan $(20,60)$ is correct?
options: It is still optimal with value 200, and $(40,20)$ also earns 200.
It is no longer optimal, since $(40,20)$ now earns more.
It is still optimal with value 200, and it is the only optimal plan.
It is no longer optimal, since $(50,0)$ now earns 200 and more.

questions.question: Giapetto's soldier demand falls, so it maximizes $3x_s+2x_t$ subject to finishing $2x_s+x_t\le100$, carpentry $x_s+x_t\le80$, demand $x_s\le15$ and $x_s,x_t\ge0$. What is the new optimal weekly profit, and at which plan?
